title: Book One · Chapter 100: The Colour at the Other End
story:
The plain end of the wooden boat is darker now.

Many small hands held it. Ronan sailed it over blankets. Once, it had a short turn in the kitchen basin. He runs a finger along the grain. He can see the thin lines in the wood.

“I want to paint it,” he tells Dad.

“Have you chosen the colour?”

“Blue.”

“The green end stays?”

“Yes.”

Dad puts the boat beside the window. It is a free afternoon. But painting will take more than a few minutes. The surface must be dry and smooth. Mum wants the table clear before supper.

They cover one corner of the table with old paper. Dad checks the rough edge he noticed months ago. He gives Ronan a small piece of sandpaper. It feels rough under his fingers.

“Lightly,” he says. “Along the wood. We are smoothing, not making it smaller.”

Ronan rubs hard at first. Dad stops him and shows one soft movement. Then he lets Ronan continue.

The work is not exciting for the first ten strokes. After a few more strokes, the edge feels different. Ronan checks it with his thumb. He turns the boat and compares the two sides.

“This one still catches.”

“Then a little more there.”

Mum comes to look. There is fine dust on the paper. Mum points to her clean cloth and the food bowls. The dust must stay away from those things. Dad moves the bowls first. Ronan sets the sandpaper aside.

They wipe the boat carefully. Dad has some blue paint left from a job. Mr Sun said, “You can take the leftover paint.” Dad checked it first. Then he brought it home. It is suitable for wood.

Ronan wants a bright blue. This blue is not very bright. It has a little grey in it.

“We can wait for another colour,” Dad says.

Ronan looks at the green end. It is not bright either.

“This one.”

They will paint after the school project is finished. Dad will help with the first coat. He needs time to watch it dry. Today they clear a place on the shelf for the boat.

There is no paint on the boat yet. Ronan feels disappointed. But he made the rough edge smooth. He feels pleased about that.

Mei's boat drawing is inside his book. He opens it and colours the plain end with his blue pencil. The shape looks different at once. He keeps the old green in its place.

At supper, Dad asks, “Shall we paint the whole boat blue? Both ends can match.”

“No,” Ronan says quickly.

Dad smiles. “Now we know the plan.”

Mum takes the sandpaper from the clean-up pile. She folds it so the rough sides face inward.

“Save this,” she says. “Small things take small pieces.”

Ronan puts it in the toolbox with Dad's permission. The boat goes back on its cloth, still half plain.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- grain＝木纹
- surface＝表面
- strokes＝几次来回动作
- coat＝一层涂料

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：sandpaper＝砂纸；thumb＝拇指；leftover paint＝剩余颜料。

## 读句提示

**Then he brought it home.**

然后／他／把它带回家。it指检查过的剩余蓝色颜料。

## 理解问题

1. 父子正式上色前先做了什么？
2. Ronan为什么坚持保留原来的绿色船头？
